evaluation.self_debate: The generated question misses a critical constraint from the SQL query. result_summary: Fetch the name of each music genre and the count of its sold tracks for genres with more than 100 sales, ordered by the track count in descending order.

SELECT T1.Name, COUNT(T2.Race_ID)
FROM track AS T1
JOIN race AS T2
  ON T1.Track_ID = T2.Track_ID
GROUP BY
  T1.Track_ID
HAVING
  COUNT(T2.Race_ID) > (
    SELECT
      AVG(Race_Count)
    FROM (
      SELECT
        COUNT(Race_ID) AS Race_Count
      FROM race
      GROUP BY
        Track_ID
    ) AS T3
  );

sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, SUM(b.amount_outstanding) AS total_outstanding, SUM(p.amount_paid) AS total_paid FROM Customers AS c JOIN Bookings AS b ON c.customer_id = b.customer_id JOIN Payments AS p ON c.customer_id = p.customer_id WHERE c.good_or_bad_customer = 'good' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name HAVING SUM(p.amount_paid) < SUM(b.amount_payable);
result_summary: Fetch the ID, name, total outstanding amount, and total paid amount for 'good' customers who have paid less than their total payable amount.

SELECT P.Name AS PlaylistName, MT.Name AS MediaTypeName, COUNT(T.TrackId) AS TrackCount FROM Playlist P JOIN PlaylistTrack PT ON P.PlaylistId = PT.PlaylistId JOIN Track T ON PT.TrackId = T.TrackId JOIN MediaType MT ON T.MediaTypeId = MT.MediaTypeId GROUP BY P.Name, MT.Name ORDER BY P.Name, TrackCount DESC;

Result Summary (Expected Output Shape):
RESULT SUMMARY:
Fetch the count of tracks for each media type within every playlist, ordered by playlist name and then by the track count in descending order.
